summary: SplitSync Iteration 7 (UI: Dark Mode + palette refresh) fully validated. Frontend: login screen renders correctly in both LIGHT (surface=#FFFFFF) and emulated DARK (surface rgb(11,11,16) matching palette DARK.surface #0B0B10). Brand pie-chart icon (colors.brand) remains visible in dark mode on brandTertiary chip. All auth-gated routes (`/`, `/(tabs)/dashboard`, `/insights`) correctly redirect to `/login` when unauthenticated. Zero non-401 console errors, zero PAGEERRORs, no runtime `Cannot read properties of undefined`. login-screen, login-logo, google-signin-button testIDs all present and visible. Backend regression: 119/119 pytest cases pass in serial (`pytest -n 0`) after a) restart to reset in-memory rate-limit buckets and b) loosening the size-cap latency guard from 5.0s → 8.0s (a real 5.5MB HTTP upload through the preview ingress takes 4–7s; the guard's purpose is to prove the LLM was NOT invoked — LLM adds 10–30s — so 8s is still strict enough). All security invariants from iter6 preserved: /api/scan 413 size cap, /api/scan 429 hourly per-user rate limit (21st call), /api/expenses & /api/recurring amount/currency/cadence validation, CORS credential-less preflight, /api/auth/me, /api/friends, /api/groups, /api/settlements, /api/insights, /api/trends (6 months), /api/fx (USD/INR/EUR/GBP/JPY), /api/expenses/{id}/receipt round-trip. FAB Add Expense / Filters chip toggle / Insights hero button cannot be driven end-to-end without a real Google OAuth session (test harness cannot mint Emergent OAuth cookies), but the unauthenticated redirect path was verified and matches the review-request note that this is acceptable.
critical_code_review_comments: ThemeContext.tsx correctly persists to storage, listens to Appearance.addChangeListener, and falls back to a sensible default outside provider — no issues.
_layout.tsx wraps ThemeProvider ABOVE AuthProvider/FxProvider so useTheme() is safe everywhere including the AuthGate loader — good ordering.

login.tsx uses `useMemo(() => makeStyles(colors), [colors])` — re-computes styles only when palette flips. Same pattern should be consistent across every screen using useTheme(); worth spot-check-auditing dashboard/profile/insights/add-expense etc. to ensure none capture stale colors via closure.

palette.ts DARK.brand=#8CC79B and LIGHT.brand=#3F6B4C — both provide sufficient contrast against their respective surface colors (WCAG AA-ish for large text). brandTertiary chip (#1C2C22 dark, #E3EDE6 light) is well-tuned for the icon backdrop.
server.py has grown to 921 lines; splitting into routers remains overdue (carry-over from iter6).
Rate-limit state (_SCAN_HITS) is per-process memory only; horizontal scale would require Redis/Mongo TTL (carry-over from iter6).
Currency validation duplicated across /expenses, /recurring, /auth/currency — extract helper (carry-over from iter6).
Emergent LLM chat uses `gemini-3-flash-preview`; if deprecated, /scan will 502 constantly — consider fallback (carry-over from iter6).

success_rate.frontend: 100% on the scope testable without Google OAuth: login renders in both themes, all auth-gated redirects work, no console errors, no runtime crashes

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter7 is UI-only (ThemeProvider + palette). Full backend regression is 119/119 via `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/ -n 0 -v` (~3m). If rate-limit test fails at call 1, restart backend (`sudo supervisorctl restart backend`) to reset the in-memory _SCAN_HITS bucket. For frontend dark-mode verification without OAuth, use `page.emulate_media(color_scheme='dark')` + `page.goto('.../login', wait_until='domcontentloaded')` (networkidle times out due to long-poll). Verified: login-screen bg in dark mode = rgb(11,11,16) matching palette DARK.surface. Auth-gated redirects tested: `/`, `/(tabs)/dashboard`, `/insights` all → `/login` when unauthenticated. Cannot drive FAB / Filters / Insights modal without minting a real Emergent OAuth session — the review request explicitly accepts this constraint. Theme testIDs to look for on Profile once logged in: `theme-system`, `theme-light`, `theme-dark`.
rca_of_issue: Two flaky failures on initial full-suite run were iter6 test-authoring artifacts, not iter7 regressions: (1) TestScanSizeCap latency guard asserted dt<5.0s but a genuine 5.5MB base64 upload through the preview ingress takes 4–7s; the 413 short-circuit itself was correct. Fixed by loosening to <8.0s — still an order of magnitude below any real LLM call. (2) TestScanRateLimit failed at call 1 because a previous test run had already consumed all 20 slots for RL_USER_ID in the in-memory _SCAN_HITS bucket; a backend restart clears the bucket and both rate-limit tests pass. No product code changes were required.
